title: Immunophenotypic Detection of Measurable Residual (Stem Cell) Disease Using LAIP Approach in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
protocol: Assess concentration of white blood cells (WBCs) in the BM sample using a cell counting chamber with Türk cell staining solution.
Dissolve 10 μl BM in 90 μl Türk solution.
Mix gently and incubate for approximately 1 minute.
Fill cell counting chamber and define cell concentration.
Alternatively, use an automated cell counter to determine the cell concentration and viability.
Define volume of BM needed based on WBC count and pipet this volume into a separate regular 15-ml tube.
Add lysing solution to the tube containing white blood cell suspension in a volume ten times that of the white blood cell suspension.
Mix gently by inverting the tubes and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge tubes for 7 minutes at 700 × g (room temperature with mild brake).
Remove supernatant from the tubes.
Resuspend cell pellet in excess PBS.
Centrifuge resuspended cells for 7 minutes at 700 × g (room temperature with mild brake).
Remove supernatant.
Re-suspend cell pellet in PBS to a concentration of ∼100 × 10^6 WBC/ml.
Divide the cell suspension evenly over four FACS tubes.
Pipette appropriate monoclonal antibodies into each tube as detailed in Table 1.
Mix gently and incubate cell suspensions with the antibody premix at room temperature for 15 minutes while protecting from light.
Add 3 ml PBS to each tube to wash stained cells.
Centrifuge cells at 400 × g for 5 minutes (with brake).
Remove supernatant and re-suspend cell pellet in 300 µl PBS.
Use the flow cytometer to measure at least 100,000 gated WBCs per tube for diagnosis samples.
Save FACS data with an appropriate file name.
Use the flow cytometer to measure at least 1,000,000 gated WBCs for follow-up samples.
Use all four regular tubes for complete LAIP follow-up identification if BM material is sufficient.
Determine LAIP(s) that were present at diagnosis of AML using available tube(s) when BM cells are limited.
Measure one tube at follow-up if both diagnosis of LAIP is unavailable and there is a shortage of follow-up material.
Prioritize tube 1 for measurement if material is short, followed by tube 2, then tube 3, and finally tube 4.
Use tube 4 with the antibody for the primitive marker CD133 if there is evidence for a CD34-negative AML.
Save FACS data using an appropriate file name.
Open FACS data from the diagnosis files using gating software to assess LAIPs at diagnosis.
Gate CD45 positive cells in the CD45/SSC plot.
Set a gate on larger cells in the FSC/SSC plot to remove red cells, debris, and high FSC cells.
Gating of single cells and removal of doublets is performed in an FSCA/FSC-H plot.
Gate white blood cells according to Basic Protocol 1, step 15a.
Within the population of WBCs, gate CD45 high and SSC low cells.
Ensure that there are no myeloid cells in the gate using CD34, CD117, CD13, and/or CD33.
Use the final population of lymphocytes as an internal control to define marker expression.
Gating lymphocytes.
Gate the WBC fraction in the sample.
Identify immature blasts within the WBC fraction using a CD45/SSC plot.
Ensure that mature granulocytes or immature lymphocytes are excluded from the immature blast fraction using an FSC/SSC plot.
Define the final population of immature blast cells as shown in dark blue on the CD45/SSC plot.
Gate lymphocytes and (im)mature blasts as described in previous steps.
Check for the presence of all possible LAIPs.
Focus on the LAIP phenotype established at diagnosis.
Choose the best LAIP based on percentage positivity and specificity.
Illustrate gating steps similar to those used for diagnosis.
Define the sample as MRD positive if LAIP positive cells exceed 0.1% of total WBCs.
Use a similar approach for mature LAIPs in follow-up BM.
Mix six different antibodies in the phycoerythrin (PE) channel.
Add CD45RA antibody to the mixture.
Include CD123 antibody in the cocktail.
Combine CD44 antibody with the existing mixture.
Add CD33 antibody to complete the panel.
Assess total LSC load using the developed antibody panel.
Prepare bone marrow cells for flow cytometry measurement.
Use 8 × 10^6 WBCs (or more if possible) for measuring stem cells.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 500 µl to prevent excessively high flow rates.
Measure at least 4 × 10^6 gated WBCs, especially for follow-up samples.
Save FACS data using an appropriate file name.
Gate white blood cells as described in Basic Protocol 1 steps 14-15.
Gate lymphocytes as described in Basic Protocol 1 steps 14-15.
Gate immature blast cells as described in Basic Protocol 1 steps 14-15.
Gate CD34 positive blast cells as shown in Figure 7A.
Plot CD34 against CD38 to identify CD34 positive blasts (shown in light blue).
Identify CD38 low cells (also referred to as CD38− cells) based on the gate in Figure 7B.
Use CD38 expression of remaining red blood cells (CD38 negative) for detection of CD38 low cells.
Alternatively, use a fixed cut-off point if instrument settings and staining protocols are standardized.
Choose a cut-off of 102 for detecting CD38 negativity in the experimental setting.
Use FSC/SSC plot to gate the cluster of CD34+ blasts.
Exclude non-specific cells with higher SSC and/or FSC.
Gate aberrancies on CD34+CD38− LSC cells.
Use stem cell markers as shown in Table 2 (CD45RA, Combi-6, CD123, CD44, and CD33) to discriminate presumed normal hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from the LSCs.
Gating strategies to identify CD34+CD38− LSCs at follow-up are identical compared to diagnosis, as described above in steps 5-7.
